sam_support: Customer (acct 3241) on Private VPC reports intermittent 403s and very high tail latency. They say requests land in eu-central instead of us-west, causing auth failures and billing mismatches. Asking for quick triage.

kate_sre: Can you drop a sample request-id + headers and the IP we see on our edge?

sam_support: request-id r-8f3c; they sent curl output and proxy logs. On our edge the source IP is 18.202.45.10 (eu range). Their bastion originates from 10.0.5.12 (private). They show `X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.5.12`.

maria_eng: quick hypothesis: customer uses an on-prem proxy/NAT in hub that SNATs to a peered egress IP in EU, our smart routing picks region from source IP -> eu mappings, so it routes to eu model endpoints, causing token billing in EU and auth mismatch (keys bound to us-west).

ingrid_oncall: check whether the customer's proxy preserves any region hint header. If not, we only have the SNAT IP to go on. Also confirm whether their peered transit uses a shared NAT gateway in EU.

sam_support: customer confirms their egress goes through a central transit gateway in EU for outbound filtering. They assumed internal traffic to Redwood would be routed via their us-west path but the transit NAT picks EU egress.

alex_runtime: two immediate mitigations: 1) we can add a temporary routing override for tenant 3241 to force us-west. 2) longer term: support honoring `X-Original-Region` or a configured `x-rw-origin-region` header from trusted proxies (only if proxy IP in allowlist). Also log decision path for audit.

sam_support: customer asked for repro steps we can share. I put together this quick curl they ran through their proxy:

```
# from customer's bastion
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
     -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.5.12" \
     -x http://proxy.internal:3128 \
     https://api.redwood.example/generate
```

sam_support: our observed TCP source on edge: 18.202.45.10 -> maps to eu-central routing.

kate_sre: For triage steps: 1) ask customer to add a temporary `X-RW-ORIGIN-REGION: us-west-2` header at their proxy (if they can). 2) We will test forcing region on routing policy. 3) Capture full TLS connection metadata from our edge for that request id.

maria_eng: added: we should also verify auth key metadata is scoped to region in our DB; if auth check uses region-bound keys it'll fail when routed to EU. Alex, can runtime log the auth-check region vs chosen serving region?

alex_runtime: yes, I'll add a one-off log flag for tenant 3241 to emit `auth_region` and `route_region` for incoming requests. Will push a small change to canary.

deploybot: routing-override for tenant=3241 -> force_region=us-west initiated by kate_sre. Change id: R-20260317-01. Canary deploy starts.

ingrid_oncall: FYI I've opened INC-789 in PagerDuty and linked the account. Tagging eng-runtime + support.

sam_support: Customer applied temporary header, reported lower latency immediately and no more 403s. They still want guidance on fixing transit NAT.

kate_sre: Next steps: 1) recommend customer's network team either preserve original client IP via proxy config (no SNAT) or insert a signed `X-RW-ORIGIN-REGION` header and add our allowlisted proxy IP(s). 2) We'll add docs on Private/VPC egress patterns and routing pitfalls. 3) Follow up to remove force_region once fix confirmed.

maria_eng: note for postmortem: update smart routing decision order to prefer explicit origin-region header from trusted proxies before inferring from source IP. Also add a warning in onboarding checklist for peered NATs that can change egress geography.

alex_runtime: pushed canary logging. I see the example request-id r-8f3c now shows `auth_region=us-west-2, route_region=eu-central` — confirms hypothesis.

sam_support: customer confirmed performance normalization after header + we removed force_region flag at 1845554380. They will engage their network team to fix NAT.

kate_sre: I'll draft a short KB: "Private deployments: egress NATs and region routing" with repro commands and recommended proxy headers. Assigning to maria_eng for content.

maria_eng: on it. I'll include examples, iptables hints for non-SNAT proxy, and example allowlist snippet for `X-RW-ORIGIN-REGION` acceptance.

sam_support: closing loop with customer now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
